binary string becomes 101.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 18px;">To achieve 101, we leftshif '10' (previous sum in binary) and add current node (1) to the string.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 18px;">Here, currentSum variable stores the sum in decimal.&nbsp;</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 18px;">We have replaced leftShift operation by multiplication with div.span: currentSum = 0*2 + 1 = 1

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 575px; margin-left: 23px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.span: The reason behind the above operation is explained here:

li.span: For example, from the root node to the current node binary string is 10.
Now, when you move to the next node having value 1, the binary string becomes 101.
To achieve 101, we leftshif '10' (previous sum in binary) and add current node (1) to the string.
Here, currentSum variable stores the sum in decimal.
We have replaced leftShift operation by multiplication with 2.
